contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #171: The hypercube Ramsey conjecture.

Audit of Section 18 late-prefix transfer for the September 23, 2026 staged hypercube Ramsey manuscript. The conclusion is local and conditional on explicitly listed upstream inputs, not a proof of the main Ramsey theorem.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 171 (The hypercube Ramsey conjecture.; papers: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
There is an absolute C>0 with R(Q_n)<=C 2^n for every integer n>=0. Source: Section 1 thm:main. Unaudited in this bounded mission.
Unbounded R(Q_n)/2^n gives a counterexample sequence n->infinity, C_n=N/2^n->infinity, N<=n2^n. Source: Section 2 lem:counterexample-sequence. No rate of divergence is imposed.
In both orientations arbitrary laws of widths alpha n and n^(x_*) have discrepancy at most b=n^(-24/25). Source: Section 12 cor:deep-discrepancy, eq:source-9. Upstream input, not proved here.

Patch extraction, allocation, stable cleaning, and balanced internal profiles supply the mode geometry and cap/degree bounds. Sources: Sections 13 and 14 prop:patch-extraction-allocation, lem:stable-patch-cleaning, prop:internal-slice-solver, prop:balanced-patch-profiles. Unaudited.

The high direct and high cluster modes admit the required assignments and column-load control. Source: Section 15 lem:high-direct-assignment, prop:high-cluster-sampling, prop:high-cluster-loads. Unaudited.

Low modes have h<=log(n)^0.1, r=O(log n), d=n-O(log n) distinct critical cells, internal IDs in distinct syndrome cosets, and cell slices separated by more than log(n)^3. Source: Section 16 opening bounds and lem:late-classes-cells. Upstream input.

Each unpinned iid-typical critical cell label has marginal q_k<=(1+O(n^-3)) pi_i; critical whole cells are independent in the late-prefix experiment. Source: Section 16 lem:fresh-singleton and Section 18 experiment. Upstream input.

On initial validity, omitting any at most (log n)^4 external early inputs leaves at most exp((log n)^8) envelope labels. Source: Section 17 definition of S_v. This is a gate, not a new unconditional estimate.
For 0<=d<=n, E_uniform_X_i^2[1_A (4 integral I_x I_z d pi_i)^(2d)]<=exp(O(log n)); A retains envelope membership and nonconflict. Source: Section 17 immediately after eq:source-24. Upstream input.

On the prerequisite gate earlier path factors are bounded by deletion kernels with total multiplier exp(1000 max(1,h_i) sum_s e_v,s)=O(1); erased side sketches may then be integrated out before seeds are fixed. Source: Section 18 local-transition requirements and erasing-history paragraphs.

Uniform pool bounds and finite initial resampling yield the stated small list-failure probabilities and multiplicative local comparison. Source: Section 17 lem:uniform-pool-list-estimate and prop:initial-resampling-comparison. Unaudited.

In the Section 18 preceding experiment, the fixed prefix-moment bad event F has probability at most exp(-n^c1), for a fixed c1>0, uniformly over all fixed noncritical cell states and independent mask profiles, also with one critical cell omitted. Literal claim: lem:late-prefix-transfer.
Terminal avoidance is simultaneously possible with stated local multiplicative comparison and one-slot-pin bounds. Source: Section 18 prop:terminal-avoidance. Unaudited downstream claim.
Late assignment can be completed using the conditional injective sampler and prescribed alarms. Source: Section 18 prop:late-assignment. Unaudited downstream claim.
Joint endpoint kernels satisfy eq:source-28 with the prescribed weights and comparisons. Source: Section 18 prop:low-endpoint-kernels. Unaudited downstream claim.
The two-endpoint kernel bound and geometric partner counts imply simultaneous Hall matchings in all palettes. Source: Section 18 lem:low-two-endpoint-hall. Unaudited downstream claim.

Conditional on LPT_DEEP, LPT_GEOMETRY, LPT_SINGLETON, LPT_MASKED, LPT_WEIGHT, and LPT_DELETE, the complete Section 18 late-prefix bridge is uniformly valid, without a conditional-on-every-history exception bound or independence after survival conditioning. The independent proof gives explicit finite-parameter stopped-likelihood and final witness bounds.

After the gated pathwise deletion comparison and integration of erased sketches, every affected sketch consults one critical block of at most max(1,h_i)r cells; the witness-independent total protocol has at most n polylog(n) updates and per-block response-prefix count at most exp(n^0.4) times a polynomial factor, with broad output on all inputs.

For independent raw whole blocks, each adaptive transcript prefix is a product cylinder; raw conditional block laws factor across blocks. With at most S response prefixes per block, K blocks and cylinder cutoff lambda, the integrated probability that the adaptively queried block has raw cylinder mass below lambda is at most K S lambda. This is not a bound conditional on each transcript.

Product domination of a block tuple, low-density-prefix removal, and deep discrepancy imply uniform-witness-averaged survival ratios 1+O(m b) outside stretched-exponentially small raw exceptions, even though tuple coordinates may be dependent after cylinder restriction.

Let the raw update exception mass averaged over allowed witnesses be <=epsilon, factor deviations <=delta<1, prior survival >=kappa^m, L updates and barrier B>=1. Put a=2delta/(1-delta), M=kappa^(-m)/(1-delta), H=(1+a^2)^L(1+L B^2 M^2 epsilon). Then stopped second moment <=H and tilted output-deviation mass <=H/B+B M L epsilon+B beta, where beta is raw output-deviation mass. No pointwise conditional exception bound is assumed.

If tilted deviation mass <=eta and E[1_A (2^(a d) product c_k)^2]<=W, then the expected number of surviving deviating ordered a-witnesses is <=M_i^a 2^(-a d) sqrt(W eta), for a=1,2. This and d=n-O(log n), M_i<=n2^n yield the claimed stretched-exponential prefix-failure bound.

For finite nonnegative weights, a zero integrated linear martingale term, a pre-exception barrier, and an unconditional weighted exception bound suffice for the one-step stopped second-moment inequality. This algebraic integration step does not require any conditional-on-history bound.

Generic description-length and approximate max-information failure-transfer results do not by themselves establish the per-block integrated-exception bridge; the available whole-transcript logarithmic range n^(1.4+o(1)) is too large to absorb the stated stretched-exponential raw error.

claims.natural_statement: For finite nonnegative weights, a zero integrated linear martingale term, a pre-exception barrier, and an unconditional weighted exception bound suffice for the one-step stopped second-moment inequality. This algebraic integration step does not require any conditional-on-history bound.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace LatePrefixTransfer

theorem quadratic_identity (r z : ℝ) :
    (r * z) ^ 2 = r ^ 2 + 2 * r ^ 2 * (z - 1) + r ^ 2 * (z - 1) ^ 2 := by
  ring

theorem pointwise_step (r z a B M e : ℝ)
    (hdev : (z - 1) ^ 2 ≤ a ^ 2 + M ^ 2 * e)
    (hbar : r ^ 2 * e ≤ B ^ 2 * e) :
    (r * z) ^ 2 ≤
      (1 + a ^ 2) * r ^ 2 + 2 * r ^ 2 * (z - 1) + B ^ 2 * M ^ 2 * e := by
  have hvar := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hdev (sq_nonneg r)
  have hexc := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbar (sq_nonneg M)
  nlinarith [quadratic_identity r z]

theorem barrier_on_live_exception (r B e : ℝ) (he : 0 ≤ e)
    (hlive : e = 0 ∨ (0 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ B)) :
    r ^ 2 * e ≤ B ^ 2 * e := by
  rcases hlive with hzero | ⟨hr, hrB⟩
  · simp [hzero]
  · have hs : r ^ 2 ≤ B ^ 2 := by nlinarith
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hs he

theorem integrated_step {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (p r z e : ι → ℝ) (a B M eps : ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ p i)
    (hdev : ∀ i ∈ s, (z i - 1) ^ 2 ≤ a ^ 2 + M ^ 2 * e i)
    (hbar : ∀ i ∈ s, r i ^ 2 * e i ≤ B ^ 2 * e i)
    (hmean : ∑ i ∈ s, p i * r i ^ 2 * (z i - 1) = 0)
    (hexc : ∑ i ∈ s, p i * e i ≤ eps) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, p i * (r i * z i) ^ 2) ≤
      (1 + a ^ 2) * (∑ i ∈ s, p i * r i ^ 2) + B ^ 2 * M ^ 2 * eps := by
  calc
    (∑ i ∈ s, p i * (r i * z i) ^ 2) ≤
        ∑ i ∈ s, p i * ((1 + a ^ 2) * r i ^ 2 +
          2 * r i ^ 2 * (z i - 1) + B ^ 2 * M ^ 2 * e i) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro i hi
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
        (pointwise_step (r i) (z i) a B M (e i) (hdev i hi) (hbar i hi)) (hp i hi)
    _ = ∑ i ∈ s, ((1 + a ^ 2) * (p i * r i ^ 2) +
          2 * (p i * r i ^ 2 * (z i - 1)) + (B ^ 2 * M ^ 2) * (p i * e i)) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i hi
      ring
    _ = (1 + a ^ 2) * (∑ i ∈ s, p i * r i ^ 2) +
          2 * (∑ i ∈ s, p i * r i ^ 2 * (z i - 1)) +
          (B ^ 2 * M ^ 2) * (∑ i ∈ s, p i * e i) := by
      simp only [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
    _ ≤ (1 + a ^ 2) * (∑ i ∈ s, p i * r i ^ 2) + B ^ 2 * M ^ 2 * eps := by
      rw [hmean]
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hexc
        (mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg B) (sq_nonneg M))
      linarith

theorem iterated_bound (v : ℕ → ℝ) (q c : ℝ)
    (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hzero : v 0 ≤ 1)
    (hstep : ∀ t, v (t + 1) ≤ q * v t + c) :
    ∀ t, v t ≤ q ^ t * (1 + (t : ℝ) * c) := by
  have hq0 : 0 ≤ q := by linarith
  have hpow : ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ^ t := by
    intro t
    induction t with
    | zero => simp
    | succ t ih =>
      rw [pow_succ]
      nlinarith
  intro t
  induction t with
  | zero => simpa using hzero
  | succ t ih =>
    calc
      v (t + 1) ≤ q * v t + c := hstep t
      _ ≤ q * (q ^ t * (1 + (t : ℝ) * c)) + c := by
        exact add_le_add_right (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ih hq0) c
      _ = q ^ (t + 1) * (1 + (t : ℝ) * c) + c := by
        rw [pow_succ]
        ring
      _ ≤ q ^ (t + 1) * (1 + ((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * c) := by
        have h := mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr (hpow (t + 1))) hc
        push_cast
        nlinarith

end LatePrefixTransfer
